newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Oil ADRs rise in New York.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Oil ADRs rise in New York.

text.p: Foreign oil companies' American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) or shares mostly moved higher on Wednesday boosted in part by prospects for higher earnings.
"Today it's oil, oil and oil," said Val Kosmider, head of international equity trading at Schroder Wertheim.
Shell Transport and Trading Co Plc was up 1-1/2 to 105-5/8 and British Petroleum Co Plc rose 1-1/8 to 146-1/2. Investors expect good results from the two companies when they post results next week.

Royal Dutch Petroleum Co rose 1-5/8 to 178-3/8 in part on speculation the company's stock could split. Kosmider said the shares typically had split when they reached 300 guilders on the Amsterdam exchange, where they were up 8.40 to 331.60 on Wednesday.
France's Elf Aquitaine rose two to 51-5/8 after Merrill Lynch reported it preferred the stock to Total or Italy's ENI. Total was up 3/4 to 42-7/8 and ENI rose 1-1/4 to 56-1/2.
Advancers led decliners by 245 to 234 among 807 ADRs, and late-morning volume was 31 million shares.
British Telecommunications Plc rose 2-3/8 to 72-3/8 after a company joint venture won a German digital mobile telephone license and NatWest Securities raised its profit forecast.
Sony Corp rose 1-1/4 to 68-1/4 after the Japanese company said profits would hit a record high this fiscal year.
Among Latin American ADRs, Brazilian telephone company Telebras was up 3/8 to 88-7/8.
((--Ian Simpson, Wall Street desk, (212) 859-1879)) (c) Reuters Limited 1997
